next_question: Can within-store template-family hold-out (train on N tasks of a family, test on held-out tasks of the same family) on WebArena-Verified v2 single shopping store provide identifiable same-mechanism parameterized transfer for C-LLM-INHERIT, and does Mind2Web cross-website splits show measurable same-mechanism overlap when inspected at task-sample level?
why_next: The Director mandate PIVOT to resolve audit VF5 is now discharged: WebArena-Verified v2 shopping has exactly one store, so the parent survey's proposed cross-site 'train on N stores test on held-out stores' design is impossible on the dataset actually available for SPIDER. The frozen MIXED verdict (duplication 0.9479) is parameterized family reuse (exact copies only 0.0781), and parameterization prevalence 0.8958 with 5/5 intent-to-element mapping keeps parameterized inheritance viable but narrows it to within-store template-family hold-out — the only cross-task axis v2 offers. The most information-dense next step is to test whether that within-store family hold-out is identifiable same-mechanism transfer (the remaining C-LLM-INHERIT prerequisite) and simultaneously verify Mind2Web's cross-website splits at task-sample level (audit VF6 still open), rather than re-tuning viewport or re-surveying documentation. This avoids repeating the failed 12-store cross-site question on v2 and leverages the 49 template families discovered here.
